title: Phantom Success, Silent Failure: Auditing the Success Checkers of Simulated Manipulation Benchmarks
author: Zirui Song, Jiadong Zhang, Zheng Lu, Xiaosong Ma et al.
description: Simulated manipulation benchmarks measure policy performance using hand-written success checkers that label each episode as a success or failure. Passing an expert demonstration shows that a checker accepts one way of completing the task. Learned policies, however, may stop after partial progress or complete the task…
summary: Simulated manipulation benchmarks measure policy performance using hand-written success checkers that label each episode as a success or failure. Passing an expert demonstration shows that a checker accepts one way of completing the task.
takeaways: These findings suggest that validating success checkers requires testing both incomplete executions and valid alternatives to expert demonstrations, and motivate more rigorous evaluation protocols for future benchmarks.
In this paper, we introduce SimAudit, an LLM-based pipeline that audits success checkers against task instructions.
Passing an expert demonstration shows that a checker accepts one way of completing the task.
